preamble: Hardening of the palatal glide [j] to the voiceless palatal stop [c] is the hallmark 'glide hardening' of Cypriot Greek: where Standard Greek has a consonant + [j] cluster (from earlier /i/ before a vowel), Cypriot has an obstruent, [c] after labials, dentals and fricatives (with devoicing of the preceding consonant) and [k] after /r/. Arvaniti notes that the glide analysis is one of several; the same facts can be described as /i/ alternating with a palatal or velar stop.

examples.note: The glide surfaces as [c] and devoices the preceding /v/ to [f].
The glide hardens to [c]; the geminate simplifies to conform to Cypriot phonotactics.

sources: Arvaniti, A. (2010). A (Brief) Review of Cypriot Phonetics and Phonology. In A. Voskos & D. Goutsos (eds.), The Greek Language in Cyprus from Antiquity to Today, 107–124. https://hdl.handle.net/2066/221088
